operational_definition: An identifiable entity undergoes visible translation across 2D image coordinates between early and late observations without necessarily altering its internal physical state.
kinematic_signature: Steady monotonic cosine drift (drift_8 > 0.25), moderate inter-frame S_t in [0.80, 0.92].
research_role: Differentiates spatial movement from stationary objects; tests basic visual motion tracking.
primary_action_classes: Pushing something from left to right; Pushing something from right to left; Moving something away from the camera; Moving something towards the camera; Picking something up; Putting something down

operational_definition: The semantic identity of the action depends strictly on the forward chronological direction of time. Reversing frame order inverts the action class into its reciprocal inverse.
kinematic_signature: Asymmetric dot product trajectories; reversal drop > 15 pp; flip rate > 30%.
research_role: Core causal probe for chronological order sensitivity and arrow of time.
primary_action_classes: Moving something towards the camera; Moving something away from the camera; Pushing something from left to right; Pushing something from right to left; Rotating something clockwise; Rotating something counter-clockwise; Turning the camera left while filming something; Turning the camera right while filming something

symbolic_condition: S(t) in S_init -> S(t') in S_final
operational_definition: An entity undergoes a distinct physical, morphological, or configuration change between early frames and late frames, transitioning between mutually exclusive states.
kinematic_signature: Sharp drop in consecutive cosine similarity S_t (< 0.75) localized at critical transition frame t_crit.
research_role: Explains major temporal rescues (86.7% rescue in state transition classes).
primary_action_classes: Opening something; Closing something; Covering something; Uncovering something; Standing something upright; Tipping something over

operational_definition: Intentional physical manipulation involving contact, containment, detachment, or placement between a human agent (hand/effector) and one or more target objects.
kinematic_signature: Trajectory inflection point when contact occurs; localized representation variance spike.
research_role: Primary driver of real-world egocentric and manipulation action understanding.
primary_action_classes: Putting something into something; Taking something out of something; Putting something on top of something; Taking something off of something; Picking something up; Putting something down

operational_definition: Motion where the position of a target object changes relative to a secondary reference entity (container, secondary object, or moving camera coordinate frame).
kinematic_signature: Differential embedding drift between foreground and background patches.
research_role: Disentangles camera egomotion from object manipulation.
primary_action_classes: Turning the camera left while filming something; Turning the camera right while filming something; Putting something into something; Taking something out of something; Putting something on top of something; Taking something off of something

symbolic_condition: Event_A prec Event_B != Event_B prec Event_A
operational_definition: A structured action composed of multiple sequential sub-phases that must occur in a fixed chronological order to constitute the action category.
kinematic_signature: Multi-phase trajectory with multiple critical frame boundaries; massive drop under shuffle.
research_role: Explains why temporal GRU vastly outperforms single frames and mean pooling on complex interactions.
primary_action_classes: Taking something out of something; Putting something into something; Taking something off of something; Putting something on top of something; Picking something up

operational_definition: Visual sequence where visual content is nearly static across frames; minimal or zero motion, interaction, or state change occurs. Serves as a vital negative control.
kinematic_signature: Consecutive cosine similarity S_t > 0.95 across all t; cumulative drift < 0.08.
research_role: Scientific negative control; verifies that temporal models do not hallucinate temporal benefit on static scenes.
primary_action_classes: Negative control across all classes (held static pauses, stationary pre-action frames)

operational_definition: Individual isolated frames do not contain sufficient visual evidence to discriminate the action label from reciprocal classes, but chronological sequence trajectory resolves the ambiguity.
kinematic_signature: Single-frame prediction entropy is high (> 2.0); GRU confidence jumps > +0.30.
research_role: Directly explains why Model A (Single) = 8.78% fails while Model C (GRU) = 34.78% succeeds.
primary_action_classes: Opening something; Closing something; Moving something away from the camera; Moving something towards the camera; Pushing something from left to right; Pushing something from right to left; Covering something; Uncovering something; Rotating something clockwise; Rotating something counter-clockwise
